name: Savvy Nomad
description: "American infrastructure for people who don't live in America anymore." Customers get a residential street address in Florida or Texas that works for banking, a driver's licence and legal mail. On top of that come guided domicile setup (Declaration of Domicile, vehicle registration), compliance alerts, mail forwarding/scanning, a Florida registered agent and staff-CPA access on the mid tier (company-stated).

mentions.evidence: Self-reported. The founder showed a Stripe dashboard on camera in a May 2026 episode. It was not independently checked. MRR $140,000 · ARR ~$1.7M · 1,400+ customers · 120–150 new customers per month 6 employees · ~$10M state taxes saved for customers (company-stated) Pricing (company-stated, pricing page): Basic Domicile $60/mo, SavvyNomad $90/mo (most popular), Domicile Premium $265/mo (+$500 one-off lease agreement)

sources.label: Starter Story episode "I Make $1.7M/Year In The Most Boring Niche Imaginable"

mentions.indieAngle: It's a regulatory-arbitrage subscription where the product is an address plus forms. A European version would serve Poles who left for the UK/NL/DE and still get letters from US/ZUS/banks: a Polish address, e-Doręczenia/ePUAP mail handling and a "prove you're non-resident" paperwork pack at 49–99 zł/mo.

whyItPrints: It's a subscription for paperwork plus a mailbox. Expats who keep a high-tax state domicile can owe state income tax for nothing, and the site pitches "save up to 14.8% of your annual income". So a $90/mo plan is a rounding error next to the tax it saves. Customers prepay ("net volume slightly higher cuz we charge people up front").
whyThisMatters:
Americans who live abroad still get mail, still need a bank, and can still owe state tax if the old state thinks they never left. Savvy Nomad sells a residential street address in Florida or Texas, plus the domicile paperwork, mail scanning, and, on the middle plan, a person who can talk tax.

The plans on the pricing page are a basic address, the popular middle plan, and a premium plan with a one-off lease agreement. Customers pay up front. The founder says more than a thousand people are on it, and that a hundred-plus join in a typical month. Six people work there. He showed a Stripe dashboard on camera in a May 2026 episode. I did not log in and check it. The number is his.

You pay so the old state stops treating you as if you still live there.
